input.claim_text: On 9 February 2024 I woke up to find someone had spray-painted graffiti all over our front fence and garage door overnight. It looks like it happened while we were asleep since there was nothing there when we went to bed. I haven't had anyone come out to quote on repainting or replacing the panels yet, so I don't have a cost figure at this stage.

output.cause: unknown person spray-painted graffiti on front fence and garage door overnight

input.query: Is graffiti/vandalism damage to fences and garage doors covered?

output.answer:
Based on the provided excerpts, I cannot fully answer this question.

The excerpts confirm that the NRMA Landlord PDS covers loss or damage from a "deliberate or intentional act (including vandalism..." [NRMA Landlord PDS, page 12], which would generally include graffiti/vandalism damage. However, the text describing this coverage is cut off mid-sentence, so I cannot confirm the full scope, conditions, or any exclusions that may apply to this benefit.

Additionally, regarding fences specifically, the excerpts note under the "Impact" listed event that there is no cover for "gates, fences or free-standing walls if the loss or damage was caused because they are not structurally sound or well-maintained" [NRMA Landlord PDS, page 14]. This exclusion relates to impact damage, not necessarily vandalism, and it is unclear from the excerpts whether this same exclusion or a similar one applies to the "Deliberate or intentional act" listed event.

There is no mention in the excerpts of garage doors in relation to vandalism or graffiti coverage.

**In summary:** The excerpts indicate vandalism is a covered cause of loss under the NRMA Landlord PDS, but there is insufficient information to confirm whether graffiti damage specifically to fences and garage doors is covered, excluded, or subject to conditions (such as the structural soundness/maintenance requirement noted for fences under a different listed event). I recommend consulting the full "Deliberate or intentional act" section of the PDS, which is not fully included in these excerpts.
